newsitem.title: USA: US spot MTBE relatively flat through week.
newsitem.headline: US spot MTBE relatively flat through week.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices were relatively flat this week despite the rise and fall of NYMEX gasoline and heating oil futures, players said on Thursday.
The slow trade is due largely to a two cent spread between conventional and reformulated gasoline, which makes it uneconomical for many refineries to buy MTBE for blending.
"Buyers aren't hungry, it's a stalemate," a trader said.
Meanwhile, the West Coast market is heard to finally be satiated after buying up barrels from the Gulf Coast to meet demand for its CARB-grade reformulated gasoline (RFG).
"The only demand I see coming in the near future is from the East Coast," said one U.S. trader.
The East Coast is starting to prepare for its winter oxy-RFG fuel season. Oxy-RFG contains about 15 percent MTBE by volume, compared to just 11 percent for regular RFG.
In New York Harbor, spot MTBE was assessed on Thursday at 91.75/92.50 cents, after 130,000 barrels were heard done early this week at 94 cents by a buyer who upgraded RFG to oxy-RFG.
On the U.S. Gulf Coast, Houston spot MTBE was valued between 88.00 cents and 89.00 cents a gallon, largely unch.
A large Gulf producer was also rumoured to have postponed a turnaround scheduled for October until November.
The rumour could not be immediately confirmed.
